findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical pair of reverse multi-source breadth-first searches. Its boundary sets, reached state, queue, row and column coordinates, and intersection are precise graph concepts, and the implementation is concise without obscuring the flow reversal. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 417 and its Python pacificAtlantic surface. The Reference preserves the island and ocean geometry, cardinal non-increasing water flow, both explained source examples, all four constraints, and an accessible path table equivalent to the source illustration.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064751541. Its dimensions, reverse-reachable helper, four-neighbor nondecreasing condition, two ocean boundary seed sets, intersection, and row-major coordinate emission are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the LeetCode wrapper and annotations.

The legal 3-, 6-, and 12-square flat plateaus span 4x in side length and 16x in cell count, forcing complete reachability. The current source passes all 11 executions at +0.01 relative growth and 1.02x; correct downhill flooding from every cell passes every output but fails only scaling at +2.37 and 75.06x.

The Approach derives reverse nondecreasing reachability, specifies both multi-source boundaries, proves the one-to-one correspondence with downhill ocean paths, and explains set intersection. It accurately states O(rc) time and O(rc) space.

The hash-bound public Reference retains the full ocean-border and water-flow model, both source examples and explanations in order, all seven first-example path witnesses, all four constraints, and a table preserving the information in the source illustration.
